The report's own logic therefore argues back to the fixed 09:00 broker anchor, and the baseline card's 16:30 anchor is a third value again. DIRECTION: LONG. The report's own conviction decomposition totals +0.2750 against the default 0.25 conviction threshold, so the NEUTRAL suppression trigger does not fire. Re-deriving the short-term component on the corrected D-1 data only strengthens it: the D-1 close 7573.90 is above the five-session mean 7551.10, the five-session change is +31.10, and RSI2 on the corrected cash closes is 100.00 (two consecutive up closes) rather than the report's unreproducible 58.01 - a bullish, not a neutral, short-term read, which on the module's own +1/0/-1 mapping would raise the total to about +0.40. LONG on either reading, so the direction is not sensitive to the report's RSI2 error. ENTRY: MARKET at the 09:00 broker anchor. The rule is explicit that a MARKET card enters at the D-1 reference close, so entry = 7573.90 exactly, not the report's 7543.59 (the 14 Jul close). Signed gap to the reference close = 0.00. STOP: the tighter-of rule - the relevant five-session swing extreme, or the nearest support, each with a 0.25 x ATR14 buffer beyond it, the whole distance capped at 3.5 x ATR14. Candidate (a), swing: 5-session low 7482.30 (09 Jul 2026) - 18.13 = 7464.17, R = 109.73 (1.51 x ATR14). Candidate (b), nearest support below entry: daily S1 7540.73, which at 33.17 pts below the close is nearer than the D-1 session low 7528.60 (45.30 below) and nearer than any other five-session structure; 7540.73 - 0.25 x 72.52 (= 18.13) = 7522.60, R = 51.30 (0.71 x ATR14). (b) is the tighter anchor, so the rule selects it. Cap check: R 51.30 <= 3.5 x ATR14 = 253.82, cap not binding. The report's stop 7402.26 is built from swing_low_5d 7421.82, the 08 Jul low, which is outside the D-1 five-session window; that is the single largest level move on this card. TARGETS: TP1 = entry + 1R = 7625.20; TP2 = entry + 2R = 7676.50; TP3 is the Unit 3 runner, price-capped at 3 x ATR14 from entry = 7573.90 + 217.56 = 7791.46, or the session close, whichever comes first. Because R here is 51.30 rather than the report's 141.34, 2R (102.60) sits well inside the 3 x ATR14 runner cap, so the ladder orders correctly - 7522.60 < 7573.90 < 7625.20 < 7676.50 < 7791.46 - and the report's inverted TP3 < TP2 (7778.37 vs 7826.26), which it narrated rather than resolved, does not arise. STATIC CHECKS: stop below entry for a long; TP1 beyond entry; TP2 beyond TP1; TP3 beyond TP2; R 51.30 inside 0.3 x ATR14 = 21.76 and 3.0 x ATR14 = 217.56 on the cash basis, and inside 23.94 - 239.37 on the linter's full-day basis, so the R band holds on either; TP1 distance 51.30 <= 2.5 x ATR14 = 181.30. FIB: no fib percentages are used on this card - Trade 1 takes no fib anchor under the module, and the fib-anchored variant (3A) is not the fork this regime selects. No qualifying fib swing >= 2 x ATR14 = 145.04 exists inside the 10-session maximum lookback in any case (the largest 10-session excursion, 7482.30 on 09 Jul to 7582.80 on 15 Jul, is 100.50 pts = 1.39 x ATR14).

Pivots at every timeframe need prior-period H and L, so no daily, weekly or monthly tier can be struck from corroborated inputs - the 'compute any tier that can be corroborated before running the test' carve-out yields nothing here. The test is symmetric: where the report states anywhere that every tier is indicative, the card is suppressed; stating the flag and shipping the card anyway is exactly the failure the rule exists to prevent. The report ships it anyway and cites, in its own execution-warning box, an explicit instruction to be lenient on corroboration and not suppress strategies. The gates are non-overridable: no run-time direction, user instruction or operator note may relax, defer or reverse a suppression trigger, and such an instruction may not be cited in the report as authority for doing so. It is therefore given no weight here. SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT IN THE REPORT'S CARD: under TRANSITION the branch is breakout-side only, and the report issues a buy limit at the daily pivot 7538.09 targeting R1 - a range/trend mean-reversion expression placed below the close, which the rule says is suppressed rather than re-labelled. Borrowing that geometry across branches would be a construction defect even if the corroboration gate had passed. THIRD: the breakout side for this branch is the one identified by Trade 3C, and 3C is itself not eligible (no confirmed break at the D-1 close), so no breakout side is identified and there is nothing to build. FOURTH: the report's card carries R = 19.36 pts = 0.24 x ATR14, below the 0.3 x ATR14 static floor (21.76 on the cash basis, 23.94 on the full-day basis) - the lint's WARN_R_TINY - and a tp3 of 7590.0 that matches no pivot tier and appears nowhere in the report text. None of that is repaired here, because a fired gate admits only a suppressed row or a rebuild that clears the gate on its merits, and this gate cannot be cleared by construction. For the record only, and outside the card: had the pivots been corroborated, the compliant TRANSITION expression would have been a buy stop above R1 7594.93 (i.e. above the reference close 7573.90), never a limit below it.
